Historical-publication compatibility, required to be resolved from exact contract mechanics rather than assumed: PublicationInputBindingService::verifyBoundContext() (shared by Seal and Reader) was read in full; its per-component check compares only a component's own stored payload_hash against its own stored semantic_payload_json -- it never re-derives a component's expected content from current config or current code. This makes the answer IMPLEMENTATION_DERIVABLE (not a fork needing a further owner decision): an old-shape registry_versions capture, lacking eligibility_contract_version entirely, verifies exactly as well as a new one and must remain VERIFIED, never BLOCKED. Proven directly by a new test, B18BeforeSealValidationTest::test_reader_verifies_a_registry_versions_capture_predating_eligibility_contract_version, which hand-inserts (via RunInputCaptureRepository::capture(), a legitimate first-time insert, never blocked by the DB's append-only immutability triggers) a registry_versions capture built from the pre-this-finding payload shape into a real, otherwise fully-valid B18BeforeSealValidationTest fixture bound context, then calls readBoundContext() directly and asserts status VERIFIED with registry_content honestly missing the key. Predicate review, per-predicate, not automatic: reviewing MD-S050-R0002/MD-S003-R0003 (bound to B18ReplayComparisonExhaustivenessTest, which genuinely exercises the real actualBoundInputContext() computation) surfaced a further gap the review itself found rather than assumed away -- formula_registry_hash/reason_registry_hash's extraction (scanning components for component_key === 'registry_versions' and taking its payload_hash) had never been exercised by any test with a real matching component present: the domain-isolation test (E046) supplies only universe_identity/ancillary, the registry_content test (E047) bypasses the components scan entirely, and the exhaustiveness fixture supplied no registry_versions component either, so that fixture's own baseline for these two fields was permanently the empty string -- a real, provably-red-capable guard proving the comparison mechanism generic, but never proving this specific extraction wired at all. Closed before promotion, not after: a new direct test (ReplayVerificationServiceTest::test_formula_and_reason_registry_hash_come_from_the_registry_versions_component) proves presence yields the real payload_hash for both fields, a change moves both, and absence is an honest empty value; the exhaustiveness fixture gained a real registry_versions entry matching the precedent already set for universe_identity/ancillary/registry_content. With every prior blocker (eligibility capture; live-config reads; the registry_versions extraction; historical compatibility) now closed and proven, MD-S050-R0002 and MD-S003-R0003 were promoted to PROVEN. MD-S050-R0014 and MD-S019-R0071 were reviewed on their own merits, not swept along: their bound guard, B18ReplayBoundInputIdentityContractTest, was re-read in full and confirmed (unchanged from F-013's own original description and E045's reconfirmation) to prove only MarketDataEvidenceExportService's pass-through of a hand-fabricated md_replay_daily_metrics row -- it never calls or mocks ReplayVerificationService::actualBoundInputContext() at all. A guard that never inspects the real writer cannot establish 'record-derived' regardless of what that writer now computes, so these two stay INCOMPLETE for a corrected reason (their own guard, not eligibility); rebinding them to a real-path guard, as E046 already did for six sibling predicates, is a legitimate next step but a materially separate, differently-scoped change from this finding's eligibility-version item, and is not performed here.
